claims.text: OpenBookQA is a question answering dataset modeled after open book exams, combining core science facts with broad common knowledge.
Human performance on the OpenBookQA dataset reaches approximately 92%.
Multiple state-of-the-art pre-trained QA methods perform worse on OpenBookQA than basic neural baselines.
Oracle experiments bypassing knowledge retrieval demonstrate that both open book science facts and additional external facts are valuable for performance.

evidence.description: The authors present OpenBookQA with 1,326 science facts and ~6,000 questions probing core facts and common knowledge.
Human performance on OpenBookQA is reported to be close to 92%.
Existing pre-trained QA methods performed worse than several simple neural baselines developed in the paper.
Oracle experiments designed to circumvent retrieval bottlenecks showed performance gains from open book and extra facts.

methodologies.name: OpenBookQA Dataset and Neural Baselines
methodologies.description: A dataset of ~6,000 elementary science questions paired with 1,326 facts, evaluated using simple neural baselines and pre-trained QA models.

limitations.text: State-of-the-art QA models suffer from a knowledge retrieval bottleneck in the multi-hop reasoning setting presented by OpenBookQA.

future_work.text: Solving the knowledge retrieval problem in a multi-hop setting to close the gap to human performance.
